title: Avianca — Context-Aware Flight Reaccommodation Automation
summary: Turned fragmented flight disruption handling into a human-in-the-loop, context-aware agent desktop workflow with dynamic HTML offers, UiPath execution in Amadeus, and SQL traceability.
outcomes: About 2 minutes less average handling time per interaction (5 to 3 minutes; engineer recollection)
Rolled out around 150 agent desktops (engineer recollection)
Reduced the need for direct Amadeus seats; precise license savings not independently verified
customerProblem: Agents handling disrupted bookings needed to interpret IVR context, compare feasible alternative itineraries, operate a legacy reservation terminal, and issue new tickets under time pressure.
productSurface: Dynamically composed, movable HTML modal on agent desktops
myRole: Hands-on automation architect and engineer: on-the-spot working prototype, then production workflow architecture, integration and rollout.
teamContext: Onelink BPO engagement serving Avianca in a Medellín contact-center operation; outcomes and demonstration timing are engineer-reported memories.
discovery: Started with call-center AHT, agent usability, reservation access costs, and complex flight-connection handling rather than an abstract RPA requirement.
Used an on-site leadership request as an opportunity to validate the smallest end-to-end interaction in a live demonstration.
productDecisions: Reuse passenger and booking context already captured by IVR rather than force agents to re-enter it.
Generate an HTML modal with contextual alternatives, passenger details, branded styling, radio-button selection and explicit submit, retaining the human decision.
Execute the selected action via centralized UiPath automation against Amadeus rather than requiring each agent to operate the host directly.
Handle multi-leg itinerary and connection constraints with appropriate operational checks, rather than assuming every disruption is a simple one-leg swap.
tradeoffs: This was pre-generative-AI deterministic automation; no AI model made booking decisions.
Amadeus is the confirmed reservation system; the exact underlying host/AS400 characterization remains unverified.
Reported financial savings and individual-seat licensing counts require contemporaneous records.
architectureSummary: IVR/call-context handoff -> on-the-fly HTML agent desktop modal -> agent-selected itinerary -> attended UiPath handoff -> back-office host automation against Amadeus -> booking/ticket update -> SQL records. A first working integration was demonstrated in approximately 20–25 minutes, followed by operational hardening and broader rollout (all times self-reported).
evaluation: Engineer-reported AHT reduction from approximately five to three minutes per interaction; no public measurement export is attached.
Multi-leg itinerary and connection validation formed part of the operational complexity.
safetyAndHumanControl: An agent reviewed and selected the proposed itinerary.
Changes to passenger bookings required constrained host execution rather than autonomous AI decisions.
delivery: Rapid proof-of-concept during stakeholder meeting; subsequent engineering, integration and rollout across about 150 desktops, according to first-person account.
businessOutcome: Approximately two minutes of handling time saved per interaction (self-reported); the aggregate dollar impact is not verified.
Reservation-seat licensing optimization was a business driver, but the precise license count or savings have not been audited.

evidence.label: First-person technical account (2026); artifacts and media citation pending

nextStage: Locate the publication, original AHT report, license invoices, and architecture artifacts to verify financial claims.

useCase: Before generative AI, disrupted-flight calls reached agents with information already collected by the IVR. Yet agents still had to work through alternate routes and reservation-system operations while the customer waited.

A movable, Avianca-branded HTML modal was generated on the fly with passenger context and proposed alternatives. The agent explicitly selected an itinerary and submitted it; UiPath completed the controlled host interaction in Amadeus and wrote operational records to SQL.

During a meeting with business and technology leadership, a working integration was demonstrated in roughly 20–25 minutes (engineer recollection). The value came next: hardening the solution, addressing multi-leg connections, and deploying across a reported 150 agent stations.
implementationHighlights: IVR context reuse and dynamic generation of a branded, movable HTML agent modal.
Radio-button selection and explicit submit preserved human-in-the-loop decision authority.
Attended agent-desktop workflow passed the selected itinerary to centralized host-system automation.
Amadeus booking/ticket workflow integration and SQL persistence.
validationProof: First-person account reports approximately 150 workstations and average handling time falling from about 5 to 3 minutes.
Media feature, dollar savings, exact Amadeus seat-license reductions, and reservation-host technology have not been independently verified.
knownLimitations: No public source code or operational customer data is provided.
The recollected US$2,000-per-minute cost is not used as a verified financial outcome.
Avoid attributing this pre-AI solution to LLMs or modern multi-agent systems.

evaluation: Qualitative improvements in manual handling and reconciliation visibility; no validated volume, savings or accuracy score is published.
businessOutcome: Less repetitive reconciliation and invoice handling; financial impact unquantified.
technicalOutcome: RPA handoffs between inventory and finance workflows

evidence.label: First-person engagement account; external records not yet attached

nextStage: Add representative anonymized process maps, exception taxonomy and approved before/after measurements.

The work predated the current agentic AI wave; the core pattern was deterministic business-rule automation tied to operational controls.

Human review of exceptions in finance/operations.

validationProof: Career record and first-person account; quantified financial metrics still require evidence.
